summary: Adversarially review the round-8 paper edits (any-width *2 minimum, wall family, flat single-component *3, 1/8, trims)

confirmed.quote: In the whole-board game no position with eight pawns or fewer is $\nim{3}$ \lab{C1}
confirmed.problem: The claim has no board scope, but the whole-board scan behind it covers only flat boards of width 1 to 8 and rings C3 to C8. Eight-pawn positions that need 9 to 11 files were never scanned in the whole-board game.
confirmed.evidence: research/star3_single/run_le8.sh and coverage.tsv: 190 runs, 110,276,698 roots, flat widths 1-8 plus C3-C8; le8/ has no w9+ files. Eight-pawn roots with gaps exist on 9 to 11 files (shapes (4,4), (3,5), (2,6), (2,2,4), (2,3,3), (2,2,2,2)); for example four one-pawn-per-file parts of two pawns span 11 files. T42's only wide coverage is in the sum model (sums_span9.py, one pawn per file; sums_le8.py), which the T42 verifier calls incomplete. The sum model also has *3 artifacts at 7 and 8 pawns, so it is not the model the sentence names. The verifier cross-checked only a sample of the width-8 scans (CHECKED-2 on a sample).
confirmed.fix: Scope the sentence, for example 'on flat boards up to eight files and on C3 to C8', or add a wide whole-board scan for 9 to 11 files.

verdict.reason:
The defect holds. The paper defines the model on n-file boards for any n (02_rules.tex, "the ordinary board with n files and eight ranks"), so "no position with eight pawns or fewer" reads as a claim over every width. The C1 evidence only supports narrower boards.

- The whole-board evidence is research/star3_single/run_le8.sh, summarised in coverage.tsv as "flat widths 1-8 + rings C3-C8", 190 runs and 110,276,698 roots. The scanner s3 is hard-limited to `--width 1..8` (s3.c line 612). le8/ has no w9 or wider files.
- Gap compression is why this leaves a real hole. An empty file stays empty forever, so any run of empty files can be shrunk to one. Each group needs a pawn of each colour (a one-colour group is already passed).
  - For 7 pawns that bounds the span at 9. The paper's own new sentence says so ("at most seven pawns on up to nine files, which covers every width"), and T40 ran scan_wide at width 9 for 7 pawns (7,784,820 roots).
  - For 8 pawns the span reaches 9 to 11 with at least two groups: (4,4), (3,5) and (2,6) with one pawn per file, and (2,2,4), (2,3,3) and (2,2,2,2). Eight-pawn roots at span 9 to 11 were never scanned in the whole-board game. The only wide eight-pawn coverage is in the sum model (sums_span9.py, sums_le8.py). Nothing under research/ has an eight-pawn run at width 9 or more.
- The sum-model coverage does not close the gap. The T42 verifier showed whole and sum differ on gapped roots, because the scanner ends the game at the first passed pawn while sums cancel +BIG against -BIG (112 of 3,000 sampled roots, and 3 of 150 random ones). The same sentence admits the sum model has *3 artifacts at seven pawns. The HSS theorem does not bridge it. It gives equal outcomes only for HSS positions and needs condition (E), and non-HSS positions with opposed threats are exactly where whole and sum diverge. The verifier also said he did not exhaustively check gapped eight-pawn roots. T40's wording fix ("among the scanned roots") already conceded the same limit for its scans.
- The same paragraph scopes its other scans carefully ("on five files", "rings on C5 to C8", "up to nine files"), so this sentence is the outlier. The conclusion's open question about a *3 with fewer than nine pawns was removed in this round, so the overclaim now propagates.

I could not refute it. I found no scan, argument, or paper clause that restricts "position" to at most 8 files. Nothing I saw suggests an actual *3 exists there; the gap is in the evidence, not a counterexample. I did not run a wide scan, since the 8-file limit rules out s3 and a filtered scan_wide run would exceed the time and memory bounds.

As sums of components some seven-pawn positions are $\nim{3}$, but only because a $+\BIG$ cancels a $-\BIG$ (Section~\ref{sec:sums-hss})."

verdict.reason: The defect is real, but it is narrower than the reviewer states. I could not refute the core of it. Conclusion line 19 says A and B are the only seven-pawn *2 positions "of width at most four" and that this "rests on one program [C1]". Round 8 changed 08_star2.tex (lines 114-116) to say that "a scan of every position with at most seven pawns on up to nine files" shows A and B are the only seven-pawn *2 on ordinary boards of any width, labelled C2. The abstract and intro were changed to "any width" in the same round. The paper's definition (01_intro.tex line 30-32) is that C2 means two independently written programs agree, and C1 means one program. So the conclusion now gives the same fact, uniqueness of A and B among seven-pawn *2 positions at width 4, a narrower scope and a weaker label than the body does. "Rests on one program" is no longer true. The evidence supports the upgrade. research/star2_min_wide/REPORT.md records that the T40 verifier wrote its own whole-board solver from cylcgt/pawns.py, not from the scanner. It finds exactly the two mirror classes at w4p7, none at widths 5-9 with 7 pawns, and reproduces every root count. The verifier explicitly says the 7-pawn statements can be called CHECKED-2. The width-4 uniqueness is therefore C2, not C1. The reviewer's second point holds only in part. 08_star2.tex line 112-113 says "One exhaustive scan ... gives these counts, so their completeness is C1". "These counts" covers both the two seven-pawn positions and the four eight-pawn positions. The eight-pawn count is still one scan: T40 covered at most 7 pawns, so C1 is correct for it. The sentence is stale only for the seven-pawn half, and it now sits next to a C2 statement of the same fact two lines later. This is a labelling clash, not a false number. The width-at-most-four claim stays true as a special case of the any-width claim. The wording is too narrow and the label too weak.

verdict.reason:
The defect holds, though it is smaller than "medium" suggests. 08_star2.tex lines 143-145 bound the family at 5<=n<=21, while 14_conclusion.tex line 21 says 5<=n<=26. The C2 label in 08 does not cover n=22..26. Paper's own definition (01_intro.tex line 31): C2 means two independently written programs agree. The evidence for the top of the range:

- cylcgt (the paper's engine) reaches n=12 only.
- ringeval_w is the only second program. ringeval.c line 482 rejects any width above STRIDE, and `(6*STRIDE) > 128` limits STRIDE to 21. reproduce.sh and REPORT.md line 159 build it with -DSTRIDE=21, so it cannot run n>21.
- n=22..26 therefore comes from one program, the T41 verifier's solver (REPORT.md line 27: "up to n=26 only (n<=21 for the report's C solver)").
- Below 22 that solver agrees with ringeval_w, so C2 is sound up to n=21.
- delegate/REVIEW.md line 491 banks the family as 5<=n<=21, with the verifier's solver to 26 only as an aside.

Two problems in the text:
1. The 08 sentence ends in `\lab{C2}` and names n=26, so it reads as if both programs reached 26. If read as "respectively" it is accurate about who reached what, but the C2 label then covers a range that only one program reaches.
2. The two sections disagree on the range of the claim. The conclusion's 26 carries no label and goes beyond what 08 asserts.

I could not refute it.

verdict.reason:
Real but low severity, and only partly as the reviewer states it.

Confirmed part: the paper defines "the census" as the positions with at most six pawns on F1 to F4, and Theorem "Census" is stated for that set only. The sources are 06_atlas.tex lines 7-9, 08_star2.tex lines 48-50 and 02_rules.tex line 99. The old abstract said "up to four files wide", which matched. This round changed that phrase to "of any width" but left "census". The any-width result comes from the separate T40 scan, which covers widths 1 to 8 with 2 to 6 pawns (1,648,741 roots) plus width 9 with 7 pawns. The body introduces it in 08_star2.tex as "A scan of every position with at most seven pawns on up to nine files". So the abstract now credits the wrong object.

Refuted part: the second claim is overstated. The fact itself is well supported. FINAL_TABLES.txt shows max_nimber <= 1 for every row with at most six pawns on widths 1 to 8. The scanner tests nimbers up to KMAX=64 (frontier_split1_fixed2.c), which exceeds any game-tree depth for six pawns (about 30). The T40 verifier's independent solver found 0 star-two and 0 star-three over the same roots. The body also has a sentence for it: "No *3 or higher nimber occurs in the default setting in any of these scans \lab{C1}", in the same subsection as the new nine-file scan. That sentence is only loosely tied to the nine-file scan, because it follows the five-file paragraph. The reviewer's proposed wording "no value above star occurs" would be wrong, since ups and fractions above star do occur. It should say no nimber star-k with k at least 2.

Related stale text outside the quoted line: 08_star2.tex lines 3-6 still say "width at most four". 14_conclusion.tex still says A and B are the only seven-pawn star-two positions "of width at most four" and that this "rests on one program \lab{C1}". The new body sentence claims the any-width version at \lab{C2}, and the T40 verifier's solver backs it, so the conclusion is out of date.
verdict.better_fix:
1. 00_abstract.tex, line 6: replace "an exhaustive census finds" with "an exhaustive scan finds". The rest of the sentence ("no nimber above star with at most six pawns on ordinary boards of any width") stays.

2. 08_star2.tex, new sentence at lines 114-116: tie the claim to the nine-file scan, with wording that is true for nimbers. Suggested text: "A scan of every position with at most seven pawns on up to nine files, which covers every width, extends this to ordinary boards of any width: with six pawns or fewer it finds no $\nim{k}$ with $k\ge2$ \lab{C1}, and in the whole-board game the only seven-pawn $\nim{2}$ are A and B \lab{C2}." If the label is not wanted there, instead change the later sentence to "...in any of these scans, the nine-file one included \lab{C1}". Do not use "no value above star".

3. Optional, to keep the paper consistent: in 14_conclusion.tex item 2, change "of width at most four rests on one program \lab{C1}" to "rests on two programs \lab{C2}". Also change the 08_star2.tex lines 3-6 roadmap from "on ordinary boards of width at most four" to "on ordinary boards of any width".

verdict.reason:
The defect is real. 14_conclusion.tex line 19 still reads "the only seven-pawn $\nim{2}$ positions of width at most four rests on one program \lab{C1}". That line was untouched this round (it is a context line in the patch), and it now contradicts text this round added. 08_star2.tex lines 114-116 say the scan of every position with at most seven pawns on up to nine files, which covers every width, gives "the only seven-pawn ones are A and B \lab{C2}". The intro (line 45) and abstract also now say "any width" with \lab{C2}. Width at most four is a subset of any width, so a claim the paper labels C2 for all widths cannot also "rest on one program" for the narrow case.

I tried to refute it on four grounds and none held.
- Evidence of a second program on width at most four: research/star2_min_wide/REPORT.md records that the verifier wrote his own whole-board solver from the rules. It finds exactly two *2 roots with 7 pawns over widths 1-9, the two known colour-reversal classes at w4p7. The report also says his solver covers 2-6 pawns on widths 1-8 and reproduces the scanner's root counts. So the width-at-most-four case is two-program too.
- Label meaning: the paper defines C2 as two independently written programs agreeing, with the second written from the rules alone (01_intro.tex line 31).
- Scope: the conclusion sentence concerns the same whole-board game and the same default setting as the body sentence, so the two cannot differ in what they count.
- Intent: the conclusion's open-problem item is about the real-chess oracle values. The caveat about A and B being the only ones is background, and its C1 label was correct before this round and is stale now.

A smaller stale piece sits at 08_star2.tex lines 113-114. "One exhaustive scan of 5,503,282 root positions gives these counts, so their completeness is \lab{C1}" covers both the two seven-pawn and the four eight-pawn positions. The verifier's solver did not recheck the eight-pawn count, so C1 is right for that count only. The seven-pawn completeness is C2, as the next sentence states. The line also sits two sentences before a C2 claim on the same seven-pawn completeness. The sentence at 08_star2.tex line 5-6 ("width at most four none exists with six pawns or fewer") is weaker than the "any width" result but still true, so I do not count it as a defect.

The reviewer's shorter version, without the clause after the semicolon, also works.

(2) 08_star2.tex lines 113-114: replace "gives these counts, so their completeness is \lab{C1}; our engine re-checked every position it reported \lab{C2}." with "gives these counts; that no other eight-pawn position is $\nim{2}$ rests on this scan alone \lab{C1}, and our engine re-checked every position it reported \lab{C2}." verdict.reason:
The defect is real but low severity. The conclusion (14_conclusion.tex line 21) says the wall family reaches n+3 pawns "for 5<=n<=26". The body (08_star2.tex lines 141-145) states the family as "ring *2 with n+3 pawns on every C_n with 5<=n<=21". Only n=26 appears afterwards, in "two other programs to n=21 and n=26 \lab{C2}". The repo evidence does not support 26 at the C2 level the body implies.

- research/ring_family/REPORT.md: the second program, ringeval_w, uses 128-bit masks. Its build condition is 6*STRIDE <= 128, so it handles n<=21 only. reproduce.sh builds it with STRIDE=21, and the verifier rebuilt it only at n=13, 16 and 21.
- n=22..26 rests on the verifier's own whole-board solver alone. This is vsolve.c, which is not in the repo and uses 32-bit file masks. The verifier ran it on n=5..26. I found no other record of any program at n=22..26.
- The body's \lab{C2} is defined in the intro as two independently written programs agreeing. A reader can take it to cover n=22..26, where it is really C1.
- Our engine's model is the component-sum model. The verifier reproduced it only to n=9, and the n=10..12 results are log-only. The programs that reach n=21 and n=26 are whole-board solvers. So the body's unqualified "ring *2" beyond n=12 means the whole-board game. The same paper separates whole-board games from sums elsewhere, for the five-file and C7 rings.

Refutation attempts that fail:
- The body does mention n=26, and the verifier's solver does give *2 for the report's families at n=5..26. So the conclusion is not false.
- But it widens the body's stated and C2-labelled range (5..21) from 21 to 26 with no caveat, and the open problem's wording rests on that range.

The reviewer's wording "does not carry the body's caveats" is fair. The model point is a smaller addition: it applies only beyond n=12 and does not need to go in the conclusion.
verdict.better_fix:
Minimal fix is in two places.
